useCase.query:
Add localization to this {{engine.id}} game for these languages: {{languages}} (the first is the source language). Strings: {{source}}.

Requirements:
- Every user-visible string becomes a stable, descriptive key (`menu.start`, `hud.coins`). Sentences with values use named placeholders, never string concatenation, and pluralized text has a plural form.
- Godot: a `localization/strings.csv` with a `keys` column plus one column per language, imported as translations and registered under `[internationalization]` in `project.godot`; code uses `tr()` and controls rely on auto-translate; switch with `TranslationServer.set_locale()`.
- Phaser: one JSON file per language under `src/i18n/`, a `t(key, params)` helper that falls back to the source language and logs missing keys in development, and text objects that re-render when the language changes.
- The chosen language persists (in the settings store if the project has one) and can be switched in-game: from the settings menu if there is one, otherwise a debug key.
- Make sure the UI font has glyphs for every language (CJK needs a CJK-capable font). Use a font already in the project or the system; if none covers a language, do not download one with an unclear license — ask the user.
- Fill the non-source languages with best-effort translations marked for human review in the file, and add a check that every key exists in every language.

Finish by running `pixo game verify --steps check,build,run --screenshot --json`. Fix every failing step and run it again; do not re-run unchanged code. Open the screenshot and confirm the change is actually on screen with no error overlay or blank canvas. Report what passed, what failed, and what could not run.
